messages.content: I need a round trip from Atlanta to Chicago for an exhibition opening. I have to be at the museum by 1:00 p.m. Tuesday, October 14, and I’ll return Friday, October 17, but the Friday timing is still uncertain.
I can narrow down the outbound now and keep a few return possibilities open. Is this for one traveler, and should I search both O’Hare and Midway?
One traveler. Please check both airports. The museum is downtown, and I need enough time after landing to get there before the crate handoff at 1:00.

Allowing time to deplane, collect any checked equipment, and travel downtown, I would target an arrival no later than about 10:30 a.m. Do you want nonstop flights only, or should I include a connection if it saves substantially?
Nonstop for the outbound. I don’t want a connection putting the handoff at risk. Economy is fine.

There are three workable nonstop outbound windows: an early flight reaching O’Hare around 8:00 a.m., a later departure arriving at O’Hare around 9:35 a.m., and a Midway option arriving close to 10:05 a.m. The first two leave more recovery time; the Midway flight has the tightest margin. Which should I focus on?
Compare the first two. I don’t need to arrive at eight if the 9:35 arrival still gives me a reasonable buffer.

The 9:35 O’Hare arrival should leave roughly two and a half hours before the handoff, though traffic or a baggage delay could reduce that. The earlier option gives about four hours and is currently $74 more. Both are nonstop economy flights.

Keep the 9:35 arrival as the leading outbound, and note the earlier one as backup. Now let’s look at Friday. The opening activities end that evening, but I’m waiting to hear whether I have to stay for a post-opening handoff.
What is the earliest time you might realistically leave the museum if the handoff is brief, and how late would you be willing to depart Chicago?
Best case, I could leave the museum at 4:30 p.m. More likely it will be around 6:00, and if there is a problem I may not get out until 7:30. I’d still rather come home Friday than add a hotel night.

That creates three useful return bands. A flight around 7:15 p.m. from Midway works only in the best case. A nonstop around 9:05 p.m. from O’Hare is more realistic if you finish near 6:00. There is also a late nonstop near 10:20 p.m. from Midway that could work after a 7:30 release, but the transfer would still need to go smoothly.
Drop the 7:15 option; that sounds too fragile. Can you hold the 9:05 O’Hare and 10:20 Midway choices as the short list without booking either one?

Yes. I’ll leave both as unbooked candidates: the 9:05 p.m. O’Hare nonstop for a likely 6:00 p.m. finish, and the 10:20 p.m. Midway nonstop for a later release. Fares and seats can change until one is selected.
Good. Please summarize the outbound choice and those two return options so I can send the timing to the museum team.

Outbound for Tuesday, October 14: leading choice is a nonstop economy flight from Atlanta arriving at O’Hare at about 9:35 a.m., leaving roughly two and a half hours to reach the museum before the 1:00 p.m. crate handoff. Backup is the earlier nonstop arriving around 8:00 a.m., currently $74 more. Friday, October 17 return short list: a 9:05 p.m. nonstop from O’Hare if you leave the museum near 6:00 p.m., or a 10:20 p.m. nonstop from Midway if the post-opening handoff keeps you until roughly 7:30. Nothing has been booked; the return choice remains pending confirmation from the museum.
